newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania pledges to shut inefficient firms.
newsitem.headline: Romania pledges to shut inefficient firms.

text.p: The head of Romania's main privatisation body said on Monday plans to shut 17 loss-making firms were irreversible and threatened action against managers opposing reforms.

"The list of the 17 companies earmarked for closure remains unchanged. We are determined to take all necessary measures to complete the process. And this is final," declared State Ownership Fund (FPS) boss Sorin Dimitriu.

Last week the government announced a list of 17 plants with chronic losses to be closed down rapidly in the latest phase of market reforms in line with suggestions made by the International Monetary Fund.
Dimitriu told a news conference supplies of raw materials, energy and funds to the 17 companies, which include three refineries and a heavy machine-building plant, had effectively ceased from Monday.
The new centrist government's tough stand on restructuring the country's industries apparently ends years of foot-dragging in performing the radical surgery needed in the inefficint sectors.
The move angered the trade unions and tens of thousands of workers staged protests across the country at the weekend.
Dimitriu said neither the FPS nor the government would give in to pressure.

"I want to make it clear the closure of those 17 companies is a warning sent to other inefficient firms," Dimitriu said in reference to another FPS list of loss-making firms earmarked for rapid restructuring or closure.
He blamed the managers of the 17 companies for their poor performance and failure to produce viable restructuring plans.

"I was suprised by their irresponsibility. They have a sick mentality. All their restructuring proposals include tax cuts, subsidies of tens of millions of dollars, rescheduling of their debts as well as funds to pay their old bills " he said.
Staff made redundant in the 17 firms would get compensation worth up to 12 monthly wages, the FPS said.
On Monday, reports in the local media said some managers who resisted the closure plans had refused to give banks their employee lists needed to calculate handouts.
Dimitriu said the FPS was determined to take legal steps against any "dangerous individuals" undermining reforms.
"Those who can't accept reforms should step aside. We will replace those managers within a week and we will take to court those who try to attract the unions in their actions," he said.
